items.competency: Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees (R.A. 6713)
items.stem: Under R.A. 6713 §7(d): An official accepts a ₱8,000 gift from a supplier with a pending bid. What is the proper action?

options.text: Refuse or return the gift and disclose it
Accept and donate the value later
Ask the supplier to reduce it below ₱1,000
Keep it if the bid is fair

items.reveal: Under §7(d), the proper action is to refuse or return the gift and disclose it.

items.reveal: Under §7(d), the proper action is to decline the tickets and record the offer.

items.competency: Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees (R.A. 6713)
items.stem: Under R.A. 6713 §4(A)(c): A director sits on the panel promoting their spouse to a regular technical post. The post is not confidential and is not coterminous personal staff. What is the proper action?

options.text: Participate if the spouse is qualified
Ask the spouse to withdraw quietly
Inhibit from the panel and disclose the relationship
Stay but abstain from the vote only

items.reveal: Section 4(A)(c) says officials must not extend undue favors on account of office to relatives by blood or marriage. The only stated exception is a strictly confidential post or coterminous personal staff. This regular technical post is neither, so the director must leave the panel and disclose the relationship. Staying on the panel, even without a vote, still extends the favor.

items.competency: Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees (R.A. 6713)
items.stem: Under R.A. 6713 §4(A)(c): An officer recommends a cousin for a regular vacancy in the same unit. The post is not confidential and is not coterminous personal staff. What is the proper action?

options.text: Withdraw the recommendation and disclose the kinship
Proceed if the cousin tops the exam
Recommend but do not sign the appointment

items.reveal: Section 4(A)(c) bars undue favors to relatives by consanguinity or affinity, except for strictly confidential or coterminous personal-staff posts. A cousin is a relative by blood, and a regular vacancy is outside the exception. The recommendation should be withdrawn and the kinship disclosed. A high exam score does not lift the bar.

items.reveal: Under §8, the proper action is to amend and file a complete SALN.

items.competency: Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees (R.A. 6713)
items.stem: Under R.A. 6713 §8: The annual SALN is submitted three months late with no justification. What is the proper action?

options.text: File immediately and explain the delay
File next year with a note
Submit a partial list for now

items.reveal: §8(A) requires the SALN to be filed on or before April 30 every year. Three months late is non-compliance (corrective action under §10, penalties under §11), so the official should file at once and explain the lateness. Waiting, deferring to next year or filing an incomplete list all leave the violation in place.

revisions.change: citation verified/corrected and explanation rewritten to give reasoning
revisions.prior_reveal: Under §8, the proper action is to file immediately and explain the delay.

items.competency: Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees (R.A. 6713)
items.stem: Under R.A. 6713 §7(a): A bids-committee member will be paid a commission by one bidder if that bidder wins a contract the committee must approve. What is the proper action?

options.text: Disclose the commission and still score the bids
Accept the commission after the award is posted
Refuse the commission and take no part in the approval
Let a sibling receive the commission and continue

items.reveal: Section 7(a) says officials shall not, directly or indirectly, have any financial or material interest in a transaction requiring the approval of their office. A success fee from a bidder is that interest. It must be refused, and the member must not take part. Paying a sibling is still an indirect interest. Section 9 is the divestment clock that runs from assumption of office; it is not the rule for this live commission.

items.competency: Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees (R.A. 6713)
items.stem: Under R.A. 6713 §7(b)(1): A licensing evaluator accepts a paid consultancy with a company that their office licenses. What is the proper action?

options.text: Keep the consultancy if the meetings are after office hours
End the consultancy while the office licenses that company
Disclose it and still sign the company's license
Stay as consultant but ask a junior to sign

items.reveal: Section 7(b)(1) says that during incumbency an official shall not accept employment as a consultant in any private enterprise regulated, supervised, or licensed by their office, unless a law expressly allows it. The consultancy has to end. After-hours meetings, disclosure, or a junior's signature do not remove the employment.

items.reveal: Under §7(d), the proper action is to refuse the cash and report the incident.

items.competency: Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees (R.A. 6713)
items.stem: Under R.A. 6713 §7(c): An employee copies confidential bid prices onto a personal drive to help a relative price a competing bid. What is the proper action?

options.text: Send only the totals, not the unit prices
Keep the file if the relative has not opened it yet
Mail it from a personal account so the office network is not used
Delete the copy, do not pass it on, and report the incident

items.reveal: Section 7(c) says officials shall not use or divulge confidential information known by reason of office to further a private interest or to give anyone an undue advantage. Copying bid prices for a relative is that misuse. The copy must be deleted, it must not be passed on, and the incident must be reported. Sending less of the file, or sending it from a personal account, is still disclosure.
